# Gower distance for mixed data

Distance of Gower (1971) between the rows of `x` (and `y`): a weighted
mean over the variables of

- numeric and logical variables: \\\|x - y\| / r\\, where \\r\\ is the
  range of the variable;

- ordered factors: the absolute difference of the level ranks divided by
  the number of levels minus one;

- other factors and characters: 0 if equal, 1 otherwise.

Pairs with a missing value in a variable ignore that variable. The
distance is model-free and serves as a baseline for the model-derived
distances.

## Usage

``` r
gower_distance(x, y = NULL, weights = NULL, ranges = NULL)
```

## Arguments

- x:

  a data.frame

- y:

  a second data.frame with the same columns (optional)

- weights:

  non-negative weights of the variables: unnamed (one per column) or
  named (variables not named get weight 1). Default: equal weights.

- ranges:

  named list of ranges (`c(min, max)`) of numeric variables. Default:
  the ranges in `x`, so that distances of new cases `y` do not depend on
  the other cases in `y`.

## Value

a `dist` object of the rows of `x`, or an `nrow(x)` x `nrow(y)` matrix
if `y` is given.

## References

Gower, J. C. (1971). A general coefficient of similarity and some of its
properties. Biometrics, 27(4), 857–871.
[doi:10.2307/2528823](https://doi.org/10.2307/2528823)

## Examples

``` r
gower_distance(iris[1:5, ])
#>            1          2          3          4
#> 2 0.24666667                                 
#> 3 0.36000000 0.24666667                      
#> 4 0.43333333 0.25333333 0.27333333           
#> 5 0.07333333 0.24000000 0.35333333 0.42666667
gower_distance(iris[1:100, -5], iris[101:103, -5])
```
